translation_en: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Khalid ibn Makhlad narrated to us, from Sulayman ibn Bilal, who narrated to me, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah said, “O Messenger of Allah, if I found a man with my wife, I would not touch him until I brought four witnesses.” The Messenger of Allah said, “Yes.” Sa‘d said, “No, by the One who sent you with the truth, I would strike him with the sword before that.” The Messenger of Allah said, “Listen to what your chief says. He is indeed jealous, and I am more jealous than he is, and Allah is more jealous than I am.”

‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Umar al-Qawariri and Abu Kamil Fudayl ibn Husayn al-Jahdari narrated to me—and the wording is Abu Kamil’s. Abu ‘Awanah narrated to us, from ‘Abd al-Malik ibn ‘Umayr, from Warrad, the secretary of al-Mughirah, from al-Mughirah ibn Shu‘bah, who said: Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah said, “If I saw a man with my wife, I would strike him with the sharp side of the sword.” This reached the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), who said: “Are you amazed at Sa‘d’s jealousy? By Allah, I am more jealous than he is, and Allah is more jealous than I am. Because of Allah’s jealousy, He has forbidden indecencies, both apparent and hidden. No person is more jealous than Allah, and no person loves an excuse more than Allah; for this reason Allah sent the messengers as bearers of glad tidings and warnings. No person loves praise more than Allah; for this reason Allah promised Paradise.”

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated it to us: Husayn ibn ‘Ali narrated to us, from Za’idah, from ‘Abd al-Malik ibn ‘Umayr, with this chain and a report like it. He said “with the sharp side” and did not say “from him.”

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, ‘Amr al-Naqid, and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated it to us—and the wording is Qutaybah’s. They said: Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: A man from Banu Fazara came to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) and said, “My wife has given birth to a dark-skinned boy.” The Prophet asked, “Do you have camels?” He said, “Yes.” He asked, “What are their colors?” He said, “Red.” He asked, “Are there any grey ones among them?” He said, “There are grey ones among them.” He asked, “How did that happen?” He replied, “Perhaps a hereditary trait drew it out.” He said, “This one too may have inherited a trait.”

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, Muhammad ibn Rafi‘, and ‘Abd ibn Humayd narrated it to us. Ibn Rafi‘ said: He narrated to us; the other two said: ‘Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma‘mar informed us; and Ibn Rafi‘ narrated to us: Ibn Abi Fudayk narrated to us: Ibn Abi Dhi’b informed us. All reported from al-Zuhri with this chain, with a report like Ibn ‘Uyaynah’s. In Ma‘mar’s report, the man said, “O Messenger of Allah, my wife gave birth to a dark-skinned boy,” thereby hinting that he wished to disown him. It adds at the end that the Prophet did not permit him to disown the child.

Abu al-Tahir and Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me—and the wording is Harmalah’s. They said: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah, that a man said, “O Messenger of Allah, my wife gave birth to a dark-skinned boy, and I have disowned him.” The Prophet asked him whether he had camels. He said yes. He asked their colors, and the man said they were red. The Prophet asked whether there were any grey ones among them. The man said yes. The Prophet asked, “How did that happen?” He replied, “Perhaps a hereditary trait drew it out.” The Prophet said, “This one too may have inherited a trait.”

Muhammad ibn Rafi‘ narrated to me: Hujayn narrated to us: al-Layth narrated to us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, who said: It has reached us that Abu Hurayrah used to narrate from the Messenger of Allah a report like theirs.

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: I said to Malik, “Did Nafi‘ narrate to you, from Ibn ‘Umar, that the Messenger of Allah said: ‘Whoever frees a share of a slave, if he has enough property to cover the slave’s price, the slave is valued at a fair price, his partners are given their shares, and the slave is fully freed for him; otherwise, only the portion he freed is freed’?”

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id and Muhammad ibn Rumh reported from al-Layth ibn Sa‘d; Shayban ibn Farrukh reported from Jarir ibn Hazim; Abu al-Rabi‘ and Abu Kamil reported from Hammad, from Ayyub; Ibn Numayr reported from his father, from ‘Ubayd Allah; Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna reported from ‘Abd al-Wahhab, who said he heard Yahya ibn Sa‘id; Ishaq ibn Mansur reported from ‘Abd al-Razzaq, from Ibn Jurayj, who informed him from Isma‘il ibn Umayyah; Harun ibn Sa‘id al-Ayli reported from Ibn Wahb, who informed him from Usamah; and Muhammad ibn Rafi‘ reported from Ibn Abi Fudayk, from Ibn Abi Dhi’b. All of them reported from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, with the meaning of Malik’s report from Nafi‘.

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: I said to Malik, “Did Nafi‘ narrate to you, from Ibn ‘Umar, that the Messenger of Allah said: ‘Whoever frees a share of a slave, if he has enough property to cover the slave’s price, he is charged a fair valuation, gives his partners their shares, and the slave is fully freed for him; otherwise, only the portion freed is freed’?”

Ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us: ‘Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah said, “Whoever frees a share of a slave must free him completely if he has enough property to cover his price. If he does not have enough property, only the portion freed is freed.”

Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us: Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to us, from Nafi‘, the client of ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah said, “Whoever frees a share of a slave, if he has enough property to cover his value, he is charged a fair valuation; otherwise, only the portion freed is freed.”

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id and Muhammad ibn Rumh reported from al-Layth ibn Sa‘d; Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna reported from ‘Abd al-Wahhab, who said he heard Yahya ibn Sa‘id; Abu al-Rabi‘ and Abu Kamil reported from Hammad ibn Zayd; Zuhayr ibn Harb reported from Isma‘il, Ibn ‘Ulayyah; Ishaq ibn Mansur reported from ‘Abd al-Razzaq, from Ibn Jurayj, from Isma‘il ibn Umayyah; Muhammad ibn Rafi‘ reported from Ibn Abi Fudayk, from Ibn Abi Dhi’b; and Harun ibn Sa‘id al-Ayli reported from Ibn Wahb, from Usamah ibn Zayd. All reported from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, from the Prophet, with this hadith. Their versions do not contain “if he has no property, only the portion freed is freed,” except the reports of Ayyub and Yahya ibn Sa‘id, who mentioned this wording and said they did not know whether it was part of the hadith or something Nafi‘ said himself. None of them says, “I heard the Messenger of Allah,” except the report of al-Layth ibn Sa‘d.

‘Amr al-Naqid and Ibn Abi ‘Umar both reported from Ibn ‘Uyaynah. Ibn Abi ‘Umar said: Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah narrated to us, from ‘Amr, from Salim ibn ‘Abd Allah, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah said: “Whoever frees a slave jointly owned by him and another person is charged a fair valuation from his property, with no shortfall or excess, and the slave is fully freed for him if he is financially able.”

‘Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: ‘Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma‘mar reported from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from Ibn ‘Umar, that the Prophet said: “Whoever frees a share he owns in a slave, the remaining portion is freed from his property if he has enough property to cover the slave’s price.”

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn al-Muthanna’s. Muhammad ibn Ja‘far narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Nadr ibn Anas, from Bashir ibn Nahik, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, who said about a slave jointly owned by two men, when one of them frees him: “He is liable.”

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated it to us—and the wording is Ibn al-Muthanna’s. Muhammad ibn Ja‘far narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Nadr ibn Anas, from Bashir ibn Nahik, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, who said about a slave jointly owned by two men, when one frees him: “He is liable.”

‘Amr al-Naqid narrated to me: Isma‘il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Ibn Abi ‘Arubah, from Qatadah, from al-Nadr ibn Anas, from Bashir ibn Nahik, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, who said: “Whoever frees a portion of a slave, his full release is from his property if he has property; if he has none, the slave is asked to work to pay for it, without being overburdened.”

‘Ali ibn Khashram narrated it to us: ‘Isa, meaning Ibn Yunus, informed us, from Sa‘id ibn Abi ‘Arubah, with this chain, adding: “If he has no property, the slave is valued at a fair price, then he is asked to work to pay for the share of the one who did not free him, without being overburdened.”

Harun ibn ‘Abd Allah narrated to me: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us: my father narrated to us: I heard Qatadah narrating with this chain, with the meaning of Ibn Abi ‘Arubah’s hadith. He mentioned in the report that the slave is valued at a fair price.
‘Ubayd Allah ibn Mu‘adh narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, with this chain, who said: “Whoever frees a portion of a slave, he is free from his own property.”

‘Amr al-Naqid narrated to me: Isma‘il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Ibn Abi ‘Arubah, from Qatadah, from al-Nadr ibn Anas, from Bashir ibn Nahik, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, who said: “Whoever frees a portion of a slave, his full release is from his property if he has property; if he has none, the slave is asked to work to pay for it, without being overburdened.”

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated it to us: ‘Ali ibn Mushir and Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us; and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and ‘Ali ibn Khashram informed us: ‘Isa ibn Yunus narrated to us. All reported from Ibn Abi ‘Arubah with this chain. ‘Isa’s report says: “Then he is asked to work to pay for the share of the one who did not free him, without being overburdened.”

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: I recited to Malik, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, from ‘Aishah, that she wanted to buy a slave girl and free her. Her family said, “We will sell her to you on condition that her wala’ belongs to us.” She mentioned this to the Messenger of Allah, who said: “Do not let that prevent you, for wala’ belongs to the one who frees.”

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Urwah, that ‘Aishah told him: Barirah came to ‘Aishah asking for help with her emancipation contract, but had paid nothing toward it. ‘Aishah said, “Go back to your family. If they wish, I will pay your contract and your wala’ will belong to me.” Barirah told her family, but they refused and said, “If she wants to count it as a favor to you, let her, but your wala’ will belong to us.” Barirah told the Messenger of Allah, who said: “Buy her and free her, for wala’ belongs to the one who frees.” Then the Messenger of Allah stood and said: “What is the matter with people who stipulate conditions that are not in Allah’s Book? Whoever stipulates a condition not in Allah’s Book, it is invalid, even if he stipulates it a hundred times. Allah’s condition is more rightful and more binding.”

Abu al-Tahir narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from ‘Aishah, the Prophet’s wife, who said: Barirah came to me and said, “O ‘Aishah, I have contracted with my family for nine awaq, one uqiyyah each year.” This is like al-Layth’s hadith. It adds that he said, “Do not let that prevent you: buy her and free her.” It also says the Messenger of Allah stood among the people, praised Allah, and then said, “To proceed.”

Abu Kurayb, Muhammad ibn al-‘Ala’ al-Hamdani, narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us: Hisham ibn ‘Urwah narrated to us: my father informed me, from ‘Aishah, who said: Barirah came to me and said, “My family have contracted with me for nine awaq over nine years, one uqiyyah each year. Help me.” I said, “If your family wish, I will pay it all at once, free you, and have your wala’.” She told her family, but they refused unless the wala’ belonged to them. She came and told me. I rebuked her, and she said, “By Allah, they will not agree.” The Messenger of Allah heard and asked me, so I told him. He said: “Buy her, free her, and stipulate the wala’ for them, for wala’ belongs to the one who frees.” I did so. ‘Aishah said: That evening the Messenger of Allah addressed the people, praised Allah as He deserves, and said: “To proceed: What is the matter with people who stipulate conditions that are not in Allah’s Book? Any condition not in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Sublime, is invalid, even if it is a hundred conditions. Allah’s Book is more rightful, and Allah’s condition is more binding. What is the matter with men among you, one of whom says, ‘Free so-and-so, and the wala’ is mine’? Wala’ belongs only to the one who frees.”

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Ibn Numayr narrated to us; and Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Waki‘ narrated to us; and Zuhayr ibn Harb and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim all reported from Jarir, all from Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, with this chain and a report like Abu Usamah’s. Jarir’s report adds that her husband was a slave, so the Messenger of Allah gave her the choice and she chose herself. If he had been free, he would not have given her the choice. Their reports do not contain the phrase “To proceed.”

Zuhayr ibn Harb and Muhammad ibn al-‘Ala’ narrated to us—and the wording is Zuhayr’s. They said: Abu Mu‘awiyah narrated to us: Hisham ibn ‘Urwah narrated to us, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, from his father, from ‘Aishah, who said: Barirah involved three rulings. Her family wanted to sell her while stipulating that her wala’ belong to them. I mentioned this to the Prophet, who said: “Buy her and free her, for wala’ belongs to the one who frees.” She was freed, and the Messenger of Allah gave her the choice, so she chose herself. People used to give charity to her, and she would give us gifts. I mentioned this to the Prophet, who said: “It is charity for her and a gift for you, so eat it.”

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Husayn ibn ‘Ali narrated to us, from Za’idah, from Simak, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, from his father, from ‘Aishah, that she bought Barirah from some people of the Ansar, who stipulated that the wala’ belong to them. The Messenger of Allah said: “Wala’ belongs to the one who grants the favor.” He gave her the choice, and her husband was a slave. She gave ‘Aishah some meat. The Messenger of Allah said, “If only you had prepared some of this meat for us.” ‘Aishah said it had been given as charity to Barirah. He said: “It is charity for her and a gift for us.”
